config.title: Berlin Museums Closed for Renovation - FAQ

items.q: Which Berlin museums are closed for renovation right now?
items.a: **Four names matter.** The Pergamonmuseum is completely closed. Museum Berggruen in Charlottenburg has been closed since 5 September 2022. The Zeughaus of the Deutsches Historisches Museum, with the German history overview exhibition, is closed for building work. The Komische Oper's own house on Behrenstraße has been closed since summer 2023, though the company still performs at the Schillertheater.

**The north wing and the northern central building reopen on 4 June 2027.** That is the date the museum publishes and runs a countdown to, and group tours are already bookable for June 2027. It brings back the Pergamon Altar, the hall of hellenistic architecture and the whole Museum für Islamische Kunst.

items.q: Will the Ishtar Gate be back when the Pergamonmuseum reopens in 2027?
items.a: **No.** The Ishtar Gate and the Processional Way belong to the Vorderasiatisches Museum, which sits in the south wing. That wing closed on 23 October 2023, stays closed after the 2027 reopening and is expected back around 2037. From June 2027 the collection shows a selection of highlights in one hall of the north wing, and the museum has not published which objects those are.

items.q: What can I see instead of the Pergamon Altar?
items.a: **Das Panorama, the rotunda right beside the Pergamonmuseum.** It pairs Yadegar Asisi's 360 degree reconstruction of the ancient city with masterpieces from the Antikensammlung, and it is open Tuesday to Sunday. Tickets are 14 euro, 7 reduced, free under 18. The Altes Museum on the Lustgarten holds the rest of the Antikensammlung for the same 14 euro.

**No, four of the five houses are open.** The Neues Museum, the Altes Museum, the Bode-Museum and the Alte Nationalgalerie are all running normally, and the James-Simon-Galerie entrance building has stayed open right through the works. Only the Pergamonmuseum is shut.

items.q: Is the Deutsches Historisches Museum open?
items.a: **Half of it.** The Zeughaus and the permanent German history exhibition are closed for building work with no reopening date announced, but the Pei building behind it is open every day from 10:00 to 18:00 with changing exhibitions. One exhibition is 7 euro, all of them 10 euro, and under 18s go free.

items.q: Which Berlin museum is open on a Monday?
items.a: **The Humboldt Forum and the Deutsches Historisches Museum's Pei building.** The Humboldt Forum is the odd one out in Berlin: it closes on Tuesday and opens on Monday. Most other museums close on Monday, and the Kunstgewerbemuseum, Sammlung Scharf-Gerstenberg, Museum Europäischer Kulturen and Friedrichswerdersche Kirche close on both Monday and Tuesday.

items.q: Does the Museumspass Berlin still make sense with the Pergamonmuseum closed?
items.a: **It can, because it was never a Pergamon ticket.** The three day pass costs 32 euro, 16 reduced, and covers around twenty houses across the city. With four Museum Island houses at 14 euro each, the pass pays for itself quickly if you are actually going to use three days of museums.
